ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-2-2, L.561-47 to L.561-52 and R.561-57 to R.561-60 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), implemented via Directive (EU) 2015/849 (AMLD4) and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5); Article R.123-210 of the French Commercial Code (Code de commerce) requires filing of the beneficial owner declaration with the registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS). Sanctions screening is carried out under EU Council Regulations implementing UN and EU asset freezes and the French Treasury's 'gels d'avoirs' lists.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent judicial authority in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (pouvoir) appointing the French incorporation agent or attorney to sign the Articles of Association and perform registration formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming lawful origin of funds for the initial capital contribution and the identity of the signatory

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and signatories against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanction lists, French Treasury asset-freeze records (Fonds de gel), OFAC SDN List where USD settlement or U.S. person involvement is contemplated, and recognized PEP data sets. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for (i) PEPs as defined by FATF and Article L.561-5 II of the French Monetary and Financial Code, (ii) citizens or residents of high-risk third countries, and (iii) legal structures with opaque or complex ownership; risk-based transaction verification using independent and reliable sources is required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises – official single portal: https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; preliminary name search conducted via Infogreffe (https://www.infogreffe.fr) and Data INPI (https://data.inpi.fr).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All formalities and constitutional documents must be drafted in French. The company name may include foreign words but must be written in the Latin script and transliterated into a French-readable form if necessary; it must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS-registered company name or protected trademark of another entity active in France. Foreign scripts are not accepted in the Kbis or registry entry; a transliterated French-legal name is required.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Since French corporate law does not provide for advance name reservation, the name is only checked when the incorporation dossier is filed via the Guichet Unique. If the RCS registrar (greffier) issues a refusal due to conflict with an existing name, public-order incompatibility, or absence of the required ministerial authorization, the proposed name is deemed unavailable. The company must revise the name or obtain the relevant authorization and resubmit the dossier. Where the refusal is wrongful or arbitrary, counsel may file an application for review before the Tribunal de Commerce or the President of the civil court for non-commercial matters under Articles L.123-3, R.123-13 and R.123-145 of the French Commercial Code within 10 days from notification of the refusal. There is no ex-parte extension of the 10-day deadline; a legal representative admitted before the bar must sign the appeal, and a copy of the refusal notice and any supporting registrations should be appended.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditioned acceptance in France: a virtual or commercial domiciliation address is permitted for the registered office only if it is physically established in France and staffed for receipt of official communications during normal business hours. For the PCBA contract-manufacturing industry, a virtual office is insufficient to establish commercial substance where the company performs operational activities such as procurement, quality control, or logistics. Its use as the sole French presence would be a material tax-substance risk and a red flag for banking and AML scrutiny.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated annual risk of unannounced physical inspection by DGFiP, URSSAF, or customs authorities ranges from 5–10% for a clean, low-risk PCBA contract manufacturer using a real operating address; 25–40% if a commercial domiciliation address is used without evidence of executive presence, and 50–60% if customs duty suspension regimes or bonded warehousing are applied with discrepancies in inventory records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce, articles L. 227-1 et seq. and Ordonnance n° 2014-604 du 14 mai 2014 relative à la simplification de la procédure de constitution des sociétés
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital of 1 EUR; no escrow account required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS

The directors of the Company, acting unanimously, resolve:

1. To subscribe to the shares of the Company as provided in the Articles of Association, confirming the issuance of shares for a total share capital of one euro (1 EUR).

2. To adopt the registered office at the address specified in the Articles of Association, granting the Board the authority to modify or transfer the registered office in accordance with applicable French law.

3. To appoint [Full Name of President] as President of the Board of Directors, [Full Name of Director] as Director, and [Full Name of Statutory Auditor] as Commissaire aux Comptes.

4. To grant the President full powers to represent the Company in all acts of management and administration, to sign all documents, and to perform all necessary filings with the competent authorities.

5. To record this resolution in the minutes of the meeting and to file it with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.

This resolution is adopted unanimously on [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts de la SAS including share capital, object, and governance. Have all shareholders sign. Submit the incorporation application online via guichet-entreprises.fr, including scanned copies of signed statuts, proof of capital subscription (bank receipt), and identity documents of directors. Pay any applicable fees if required (none for basic SAS). Receive acknowledgment and wait for processing.

Proof of address for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or incomplete, provide the requested additional documents or corrections within 15 days to avoid rejection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No specific industrial licensing authority for PCBA contract manufacturing; general compliance with labor and environmental regulations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: French Environment and Energy Management Agency (ADEME)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with general standards for waste disposal, VOC emissions, and wastewater treatment

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and structural inspections may be required for premises; workplace clearance under labor code

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the official portal at impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French SAS entities are automatically assigned SIREN and SIRET identifiers upon registration with the guichet-entreprises.fr or Chambre de Commerce. Foreign entities with a fixed establishment in France must register for a local VAT identification number through the tax authorities or via the single contact point for business formalities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available; French entities are subject to mandatory entity-level taxation under the Impôt sur les Sociétés regime. Limited hybrid mismatch or territorial election options may apply in specific holding structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 85,000 EUR annual turnover for goods and services triggering mandatory registration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory issuance of e-invoices in Factur-X XML format for B2B transactions since October 2024; integration with digital platforms for real-time fiscal clearance and stamping; API requirements for large taxpayers under the PEPITES system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Eligibility for 0% VAT rate on exports of goods to non-EU countries or qualifying intra-EU supplies; requires proof of actual export and non-repatriation to France or EU in certain cases.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Penalties for fraudulent zero-rating claims include fines up to 80% of the evaded VAT amount, interest surcharges, and retrospective clawback of zero-rated VAT with potential criminal prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF), operating within the Eurosystem and subject to ESCB rules; prudential supervision by the ACPR; monetary authority delegated to the ECB. France has accepted Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement; no exchange controls are maintained.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for current and capital account operations. France imposes no approval regime for cross-border payments; freedom of capital movements is guaranteed by TFEU Art. 63 and the EU Capital Movement Directive (88/361/EEC). Practical hurdles: mandatory balance-of-payments (BOP) statistical declaration, filed via the intermediary bank, for each cross-border flow exceeding EUR 50,000, and EU/French sanctions screening by DG Trésor/BdF for restricted counterparties. Profit remittance obstacles: outbound dividend payment incurs 25% French withholding tax (WHT), with 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for a qualifying EU parent holding at least 5% for two years, or treaty-reduced rates; no FX licence or prior capital-repatriation authorization applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. France does not impose export-proceeds surrender, conversion, or repatriation timelines. PCBA export receivables may remain in foreign currencies in free accounts or be converted at the operator's discretion; banks retain only the BOP statistical reporting duty for transactions above the EUR 50,000 threshold.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Compte bloqué (Capital Escrow Account) and EUR/USD Operational Accounts; trade finance desk
Capital Escrow Account, Operational Account, MT103/MT700 trade services
Operational Accounts and cash management; group coverage via CACIB for LC confirmations

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE Group (Banque Populaire / Caisse d'Épargne networks)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Accounts; regional commercial coverage with Natixis CIB for international flows
Operational Accounts and documentary credit issuance

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for daily operational payments; Low for trade and escrow rails. Licensed EMIs (Qonto, Revolut Business, Shine, Memo Bank as a full bank) provide remote onboarding, EUR IBANs, and SEPA/instant payments. Legal constraints: EMIs are not credit institutions under the French Monetary and Financial Code (Art. L522-1) and cannot open the statutory blocked formation account, issue or confirm letters of credit under UCP600, or provide import/export trade loans; deposit protection is only through passported deposit-guarantee schemes. Hence EMIs should be limited to second-liquidity accounts, never the primary settlement rail for PCBA cross-border trade.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory rule: remote onboarding is lawful where the bank performs identification via a qualified electronic signature or video KYC in accordance with CPMLF Art. R561-5-2 and ACPR doctrine. Practice: Tier-1 French banks still require at least one physical compliance interview for the SAS president and principal shareholders, plus notarised/legalised corporate documents translated into French by a certified translator for foreign entities. A power of attorney granted to a tax-resident French representative reduces the on-site mandate for signatories, but the president's biometric passport check is almost always an in-person or live-video step. Budget 3–6 weeks for onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner registry (RBE) incomplete or filed after company formation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of the RBE declaration receipt (récépissé de déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs), the Kbis extract of the SAS, the signed statuts, and UBO passports; for non-EU UBOs add apostilled copies and French certified translation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the initial share capital injection from a non-EU parent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month bank statements of the contributing shareholders, signed source-of-wealth statement, sales/asset liquidation agreements evidencing the origin of funds, draft board resolution authorising the contribution, and a business-plan justification showing the PCBA contract-manufacturing rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential sanctions exposure of the PCBA supply chain (Asia sourcing).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master purchase agreement, invoices, packing lists with HS/TARIC classification (8534 for printed circuits), Incoterms and transport documents (B/L or waybills), end-user/no-re-export undertaking, ISO 9001 certificate, and dual-use control assessment confirming that ISIC 2610 articles are not on the EU dual-use list.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign directors/UBOs without a French tax identification or visible economic nexus.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax-residence attestations from the foreign jurisdictions, group organisation chart, French power of attorney granted to the local manager, and evidence of the SAS real office (lease/utilities) and payroll registration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk counterparty payment destinations (e.g., toll-manufacturing suppliers in non-EU low-tax or high-risk jurisdictions).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due-diligence questionnaire, sanctions screening results, bank reference letters for the counterparty, contractual parent-company guarantee, and a compliance declaration under the French Sapin II anti-corruption framework where applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign parent wires EUR (or convertible currency converted to EUR) to the French bank's blocked account in the name of the SAS under formation, with the instruction purpose stated as APPORT EN CAPITAL – CONSTITUTION SAS and the notary's reference. The bank issues the attestation de dépôt des fonds enabling the greffe to enter the SAS in the RCS (commercial register). For compliance, include the UBO declaration, the bank's BOP tagging of the flow as direct investment (equity capital), and the ISO 20022 payment purpose code for capital contribution (e.g., COST or EQUI). Where a notary holds the funds, the notary transfers to the corporate operational account after RCS registration. The flow remains fully free of FX licensing; only BOP and sanctions screening apply.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (i) SWIFT MT103/TT for high-volume component payments to suppliers in EUR or USD, using UETR references and trade-related payment purposes; (ii) commercial letters of credit under UCP600 (MT700 issuance, MT720 transfer for back-to-back purchases of sub-assemblies) for large PCB/component purchase orders; (iii) documentary collections (MT400/MT420) for lower-risk relationships. French banks price LC issuance at 0.15–0.5% per quarter plus confirmation costs; the SAS should maintain committed import limits and request EUR/USD multi-currency accounts. For payments in CNY, an MT103 in EUR to a Chinese correspondent converting via onshore deliverable forwards is the standard compliant rail, supported by customs declarations (TARIC 8534 for bare PCBs, 8473 for assembled modules) and supplier contracts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable forward contracts (swap de change à terme) on EUR/USD and EUR/CNY with French credit institutions – fully permitted without prior licence, subject to EMIR margin rules.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNY/CNH with offshore counterparties – lawful in France and economically available where the underlying settlement currency is restricted onshore.
Cross-currency swaps (CCIRS / XCCY) to hedge the currency mismatch of intercompany loans in USD/CNH against the EUR-functional treasury.
FX swaps (swap de change) and forward-forward contracts for short-term liquidity and roll-over purposes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (bilan, compte de résultat, annexe) approved by the SAS shareholders and filed with the commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Court Registry of the Commercial Court)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval required within 6 months after fiscal year-end; deposit with the Greffe required within 1 month after approval, making the hard statutory outer deadline approximately 7 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to timely deposit may trigger court-ordered compliance, financial penalty of up to EUR 1,500, and persistent non-compliance can expose the company to judicial strike-off (radiation from the RCS) after formal notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and supporting schedules (Form 2065 and annual financial annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – local corporate tax office (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months of fiscal year-end; for a 31 December fiscal year-end the applicable electronic filing deadline is the corresponding date in May as published by the French tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or omission triggers a 10% late-filing surcharge on tax due, increased to 40% if the omission is intentional; a fixed EUR 1,500 penalty may apply where no tax is payable, and directors may be held jointly liable in cases of fraud

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership declaration (RBE) kept current in the RCS file following any share transfer or change in control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No separate annual confirmation form; initial declaration is made on registration and any change in UBO status or ownership above the 25% threshold must be filed within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to disclose beneficial owners may result in a fine of up to EUR 7,500 and up to 6 months' imprisonment for the legal representative; the registry may also refuse to process related filings until the UBO file is corrected

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A French SAS is subject to mandatory independent audit when it exceeds two of the three Article L823-2 thresholds at fiscal year-end: total balance-sheet EUR 4 million, net turnover excluding tax EUR 8 million, and average workforce of 50 employees; small-company exemptions under the PACTE law apply if the company falls below these thresholds and is not part of a required group audit scenario
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the Plan Comptable Général (ANC règlement 2014-03, as subsequently amended); IFRS is required only for consolidated accounts of listed entities and is not applicable to an ordinary unlisted SAS

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a standalone annual UBO confirmation statement; the company must make a responsive declaration within 30 days of any direct or indirect share transfer or control alteration. The Greffe cross-checks the RBE file against the shareholders and corporate officer data submitted with the annual accounts filing, thereby creating an effective annual refresh of the UBO record without a separate deliverable
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registre des mouvements de titres – share register and securities transfer ledger)
Register of Directors (Registre des mandats sociaux – corporate officer mandate record)
Minute Book (Registre des procès-verbaux – shareholder resolutions and assembly minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 650–1,300 (EUR 600–1,200) per year for registered business-domiciliation services using an RCS-approved provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,800–11,500 (EUR 3,500–10,600) for a small-to-medium unlisted SAS depending on asset base, transaction volume, and accounting complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit (maximum 5% of payroll), accelerated depreciation, regional tax holidays

tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 3 months after fiscal year-end (e.g. 31 March for calendar year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French-source income; non-residents file if applicable
Incorporate transfer pricing adjustments and statutory deductions
Apply withholding tax credits and loss carryforwards

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 0.5% of tax due per month of delay (minimum €125, maximum 25% of tax due)

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 12.8% (reduced to 0% for EU/EEA under Parent-Subsidiary Directive)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit TRC application to French tax authorities with supporting documentation and beneficial ownership certificate
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 5% standard rate (10% for certain IP); Interest: 0% intra-EU, 25% otherwise, reduced by bilateral treaties

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: 50 million EUR local file; 750 million EUR master file
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicable to holding companies and IP entities; requires adequate local employees, premises and core income-generating activities

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or false statement in tax return to reduce tax liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to 500% of evaded tax plus imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, imprisonment, fines and professional disqualification

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a company lacking economic substance or real business operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of income, denial of deductions, penalties up to 500% of tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for unpaid taxes, possible jail time for fraudulent conduct

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file suspicious transaction reports or comply with KYC obligations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €1 million or 5% of annual turnover, criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines, imprisonment and professional disqualification
